views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the early-October Washington round to seek a pause in further U.S. tariff ratchets (the Oct 15 lift of List 1–3 from 25% to 30%, and the Dec 15 List 4B tranche) without locking in structural legal changes or a large, one-sided purchase package. Keep farm-goodwill (soy/pork exemptions and some buying) as a tactical chip, not a final concession. Do not implement the unreliable-entity list, rare-earth export curbs, or a new tariff tranche while talks are live — those moves would likely harden the pending U.S. hikes and close the only de-escalation window now open.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Almost the entire U.S. import basket from China is now tariffed or scheduled to be: List 3 rose to 25% on 2019-05-10; List 4A took effect at 15% on 2019-09-01; List 4B remains set for Dec 15; and the 25%→30% hike on ~$250B was only postponed from Oct 1 to Oct 15 as a 70th-anniversary gesture. Huawei remains on the Entity List (May 16), with 46 more affiliates added in August and only a narrow TGL through Nov 18 — a direct hit on a national champion and on tech self-sufficiency. CNY broke 7 on Aug 5, drawing a currency-manipulator designation; spot DEXCHUS was still 7.13 on Oct 9 (+6.3% vs April). Official IP growth slipped to a 4.4% y/y August print (weakest single month since 2002 in contemporaneous reporting) and merchandise exports eased ~1.4% over the 180-day window; CPI is rising (index 107.8→110.8) as ASF/pork shortages bite. That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor (export sectors hit, FX pressure, Huawei targeting) but not +1.0: reserves are stable near $3.12T, IP is still positive, and the U.S. is also showing strain (Fed funds 2.39→1.83, 10-year 2.55→1.59, UMCSENT 100→89.8 in August). Action should therefore be mild. Mid-September deputy talks were only “constructive/productive,” China restated that any deal must remove U.S. tariffs and be balanced, and no new structural text was tabled — so this is not the moment for concede_purchases or full_rollback. Reciprocal goodwill already on the table (China’s 16-item exemption list Sep 11; soy/pork carve-outs Sep 13; Trump’s Oct 15 delay at Liu He’s request) is enough to justify negotiate rather than hold, but not enough to pre-commit purchases or laws. Further escalation would forfeit the Oct 10–15 window and invite the very tariff cascade that is the main threat.
key_factors: Pending Oct 15 List 1–3 hike 25%→30% and Dec 15 List 4B still hang over exporters
Huawei Entity List plus August affiliate expansion is firm-level tech coercion, not just tariffs
CNY >7 and manipulator label create FX/stability stigma even with stable reserves
Domestic slowdown (Aug IP 4.4% y/y) and pork-driven CPI raise the cost of a longer war
Washington 13th-round talks and mutual Sep goodwill make negotiation the least-bad path; U.S. has not yet tabled a matching tariff rollback that would justify purchase commitments

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
CNY/USD latest 7.1316 on 2019-10-09; +0.42 / +6.3% over the window after breaking 7 on Aug 5.
China industrial production index latest 104.7 (2019-10-01) vs 105.0 in May; contemporaneous Aug print 4.4% y/y was the weakest single month since 2002.
China reserves ex-gold stable at ~$3.125T (2019-10-01), change only +0.15% — no reserve-crisis signal.
Trump delayed the 25% to 30% hike on $250B of Chinese goods from Oct 1 to Oct 15 at Liu He's request as a 70th-anniversary goodwill gesture.
Mid-September deputy talks called constructive/productive; China demanded all U.S. tariffs be removed and a balanced deal; U.S. side judged they were not close to an agreement.
August industrial production +4.4% y/y, below 5.2% consensus and weaker than July; retail sales and FAI also slowed as the trade war weighed.
